question: Which of the following five year plan in India tried to build the basis for a socialist pattern of society?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Second Five Year Plan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Second Five Year Plan (1956-1961)** was aimed at creating the foundation for a **socialist pattern of society in India**.
 
• The plan focused on the **industrialization of the economy**, especially heavy industries, to reduce the dependence on agriculture and create a more balanced economic structure.
 
• It emphasized **public sector dominance** in key industries such as iron and steel, heavy engineering, and machine-building, aligning with the principles of socialism.
 
• Under the leadership of **Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru**, this plan was heavily influenced by the **Soviet Union's planning model**, which focused on centralized economic planning and state control.
 
• The plan also aimed to achieve **self-reliance** by reducing imports and building a strong industrial base in the country.
 
• The **Mahalanobis Model**, named after statistician **P.C. Mahalanobis**, was adopted for this plan, emphasizing investment in the capital goods sector to accelerate economic growth.
